seo.title: Landscaping in Highlands, BC: Tree Work & Acreage | RNC
seo.description: Clearance pruning, permit-checked tree work, well-water drip irrigation and property upkeep for Highlands forested and lakeside lots. Get a free quote.

h1: Landscaping and tree work in Highlands
cardSummary: Forested, rocky lots near lakes and slopes, mostly on wells, where cutting a significant tree is prohibited outright.
intro: Highlands is rural and forested, with homes on rocky slopes and near lakes around Millstream, Caleb Pike and Fork Lake rather than streets of lawns.

A tree cutting permit is needed for protected species and for any tree near a watercourse, lake or steep slope, and cutting a significant tree is prohibited. Many homes use wells, so CRD watering rules apply only where a property is connected. See [tree and vegetation work](/services/tree-vegetation/) or [request a free quote](/free-quote/?area=highlands).
localRulesIntro: Highlands protects native species including cascara and manzanita, and regulates any tree near a lake, watercourse or steep slope, which covers much of the district. Felling in nesting season needs a bird check.

localNotes.title: Highlands Tree Management Bylaw
localNotes.text: Under Highlands' Tree Management Bylaw No. 10, cutting a protected tree (Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood, Pacific yew, cascara, manzanita, Douglas-fir over 60 cm, any tree over 80 cm) or any tree near a watercourse, lake or steep slope needs a permit; cutting a significant tree is prohibited. Check for nesting birds before felling in nesting season.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule (connected properties only)
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply (many rural properties use wells; the rules apply only where connected): lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Wells, not the regional supply
conditions.body: Many Highlands homes draw on private wells. Irrigation works well as low-flow drip on a timer, sized to what the well can supply in late summer.

conditions.title: Thin soil over rock
conditions.body: Rocky outcrops and shallow soil are the norm. Planting suits drought-tolerant natives in pockets of soil, and lawns are rarely the right choice.

conditions.title: Brush near buildings
conditions.body: Forested lots build up dry brush, low limbs and fallen debris near houses and outbuildings, which is worth clearing back each spring.

conditions.title: Lakes, streams and slopes
conditions.body: Because trees near water or on steep slopes need a permit, most clearing jobs here start with a look at where the lot sits.

topServices.why: Clearance pruning over roofs and driveways, and permit-checked removals, are the core work on forested lots.
Gardens on well water need small, efficient drip systems rather than lawn sprinklers.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Property upkeep around the house, driveway and outbuildings.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Planting suited to rocky, dry sites and native meadow edges.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Drip systems for gardens on well water, designed for low flow.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Clearance pruning and removals after a permit check near lakes and slopes.

jobNotes.title: Brush cleared, arbutus kept
jobNotes.body: Brush and low limbs were cleared back from a house and workshop, while an arbutus that a permit check showed was protected stayed in place.

jobNotes.title: Drip sized for a low-yield well
jobNotes.body: A small vegetable garden was put on a timed drip line with low-flow emitters, run early in the morning so the well could recover between cycles.

cta.heading: Get a free quote in Highlands
cta.body: Tell us whether the work is near a lake, stream or steep slope, and whether you are on a well. Both shape the permit question and the plan.
